questions.microtag: What is your opinion, Justify, Aadhaar-Voter ID linkage, India
questions.questionText: Amid the recent controversy over alleged electoral roll related-malpractices, the debate on  mandatory Aadhaar-Voter ID linkage has regained attention. What is your opinion in this regard? Justify  your answer.

answers.answerText:
| **Approach:** • Introduce the answer by giving a brief background about the recent controversies over alleged electoral roll related-malpractices and the proposal for Aadhar-Voter ID linkage.
• In the body, provide your opinion over the proposal and justify the same with valid arguments.
• Conclude by suggesting a way forward. | | --- | After the recently concluded **Maharashtra Assembly elections** (November 2024), several political parties and civil society organizations alleged **discrepancies related to voter registrations**. They also underlined their **consequences for public trust** in the electoral process. The linking of Aadhar and Voter ID was **first tried by the EC** in February 2015 when it launched the **NERPAP** to address the **issue of duplicate entries** in the electoral rolls. However, the exercise was **suspended** **after the** **SC** flagged the **mandatory use** of Aadhar for **non-welfare purposes**. **Aadhaar-Voter ID linkage** can have the following benefits in the **electoral process**: 1. a) **Weeding out duplication** of voters so that one citizen has only one vote, upholding the democratic principle of **"one person, one vote”**; b) may ease **voter mobility**, especially for **domestic migrants**, enabling them to participate in the democratic process at their place of residence. 2. **Aadhar-based verification** of biometrics (iris scan, fingerprint) offers a more **reliable method of** **voter identification**, reducing **impersonation fraud** while streamlining the **verification process** at polling stations (using fingerprint scanner to verify biometrics). 3. **Greater coverage of Aadhar** (>99% of Indian population covered by it) gives it **practical** **implementation advantage** over other **official identity proofs** (ration cards, driving licenses) for validation of electoral roll entries. 4. a) Aadhar-Voter ID linkage will also help **fulfill the legislative intent** expressed in Election Laws Amendment Act 2021; b) can act as the springboard for **future innovations** (remote voting, e-voting) that can improve **participation rates**. However, there exist the following concerns with regards to **mandatory Aadhaar-Voter ID linkage**: 1. a) Apprehensions about **violation of informational autonomy** (little choice in deciding the official document they wish to use) and **privacy** (absence of a robust data protection framework); b) Aadhaar verifies **residence rather than citizenship**, creating a **fundamental mismatch** with voter eligibility requirements that primarily depend on **citizenship status.** 2. Possibility of high levels of **exclusion errors** (e.g. disenfranchisement of 3 mn voters in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in 2015), especially among **vulnerable sections**. This would infringe upon their constitutional **right to vote**. 3. a) The Supreme Court's **KS Puttaswamy judgment** placed restrictions on mandatory Aadhaar usage, making **blanket implementation** legally questionable; b) **centralization** of electoral and demographic data creates risks of **political misuse**(voter profiling) through **targeted voter suppression or** **manipulation** While there are **multiple benefits** of Voter ID-Aadhar linkage, the **disadvantages necessitate a pause** in the process. This pause should be utilized to generate **voter awareness** about the benefits of this exercise and **remove infirmities in the Aadhar database**. At the same time, suitable **safeguards** should be instituted **to** **prevent misuse**. (***405 words***) **Additional resource:** A move that endangers the right to vote - The Hindu
